subject: Geopolitics
title: Middle East Water Crisis
description: A short lesson to help you apply Middle East Water Crisis.

hook.text: Jordan is the second most water-scarce country on Earth. Its population has quadrupled since 1970.

buildup.text: The Middle East has 5% of the world's population and 1% of its fresh water. The math doesn't work.

discovery.text: Israel, Jordan, and Palestine share the Jordan River and aquifers beneath the West Bank. Each claims more than exists.

twist.text: Israel uses desalination to solve its shortage. Poorer neighbors can't afford the same technology at scale.

climax.text: Water scarcity in the Middle East will get worse. Climate models predict 25% less rainfall by 2050.

punchline.text: Oil made the Middle East rich. Water may unmake it.

quiz.question: How does the Middle East's population compare to its fresh water supply?
options: 5% of world population, 1% of fresh water
10% of world population, 5% of fresh water
2% of world population, 3% of fresh water
